questions.question: How did you get into tech?
questions.answer: I've been interested in computers since I was a kid, but aviation was where I began my career. I later studied UX design and moved into frontend engineering. Having worked in both design and development helps me think about the whole product.

questions.question: What did you learn from UX?
questions.lead: To understand the problem before designing a screen.
questions.answer: I learned to ask what someone is trying to do, what they need to know, and where they might get stuck. I still ask those questions when I'm building an interface.

questions.question: Why did you move into frontend?
questions.lead: I wanted to build my own designs.
questions.answer: I enjoyed UX, but I wanted to work on the implementation too. Frontend gave me the chance to build the interactions, handle loading and error states, and see a feature through from start to finish.

questions.question: What do you do at F24?
questions.lead: I build software for critical situations.
questions.answer: I've spent four years at F24 working on crisis management and critical communication software. I built the original Svelte frontend, and now I work in React. It matters that the information is clear and the interface stays reliable when people need it.

scene.caption: An example of a crisis management workflow

questions.question: What details do you care about?
questions.lead: The things that make a product reliable.
questions.answer: If a request fails, the data already on screen should stay there. A slow response shouldn't overwrite newer results. Closing a panel should return keyboard focus to the right place. They're not big visual features, but they make an interface much easier to use.

questions.question: What do you build in your spare time?
questions.lead: I also work on my own products.
questions.answer: Second Voice is a writing tool that shows what changed in a rewrite. Flow turns spoken requests into editable actions. I've also built Leu, focused on reading and learning, and Needle, an artwork search project. I enjoy being able to design and build the whole thing myself.

scene.caption: Examples from Second Voice and Flow

questions.question: What do you like learning about?
questions.lead: How things work behind the screen.
questions.answer: I like understanding the technical details behind things we use every day. DNS, TLS and what happens when you open a website are good examples. I also enjoy turning those explanations into interactive demos.

scene.caption: What happens during a web request

questions.question: What matters to you when writing code?
questions.answer: I care about accessibility, performance, tests and code that's easy for someone else to maintain. I don't want a project to be hard to use or hard to change because I rushed the implementation.

ending.label: Contact
ending.question: Want to talk?
ending.answer: If you'd like to discuss my work, have a question or want to talk about a project, feel free to get in touch.

Hi, I'm Miguel Almeida.

I've been interested in computers since I was a kid. I started my career in aviation, then moved into UX design and frontend engineering.

I'm based in Berlin and work at F24 on crisis management and critical communication software. I built the original Svelte frontend and now work in React.

I also build my own projects, including Second Voice, Flow, Leu and Needle.

miguelalmeida1592@gmail.com
